Read the passage below and then answer questions 6 to 9.

All animals in the forest feared the cock. This was because they believed the red comb on cock’s
head was fire.

“If you make me angry, I will burn you,” he often told the animals.

One afternoon, it rained heavily. The animals felt very cold. They wanted to light a fire to keep
themselves warm. Unfortunately, all the matchsticks were wet.

“T have an idea,” said Monkey, “Let us ask the cock to light the fire for us.” All the other
animals agreed this was a bright idea. They went to look for the cock. They found him sleeping on a
branch of a tree.

“Psst, that is better,” said Monkey. He then took a stick and placed it slowly on the cock’s
comb. Nothing happened. The monkey blew on the comb hoping that the stick would start to burn.
Suddenly, the cock awoke. He was surprised to see the animals around him. He realised his lie had been
discovered. “There is no fire on your head!” shouted Hare.

“Yes, you have been cheating us!” Monkey added. The cock broke off from the animals and ran
to a nearby village. Since then he lives with human beings.

Read the story below and then answer questions 10 to 12.

Human beings believe they are better than animals. This is because they are able to do many
things which animals cannot even dream of doing.

However, do you know that there are things some animals can do much better than us? Dogs, for
example, can smell better than us. They have a sharp sense of smell. No wonder they are used to detect
drugs, weapons and other substances that could harm us.

Cats are able to see clearly in the dark, something we humans cannot do. This enables the cat to
hunt at night. The animal also has a good hearing ability. It is able to hear very soft sounds which the
human ear cannot detect.

An eagle up in the sky can see a rabbit more than three kilometres on the ground below. The bird
has a very strong eyesight which is much better than that of human beings. Indeed, the different abilities
of human beings and animals make the earth an interesting place to live in.

Read the passage below and then answer questions 13 to 15.

Malaria is responsible for many deaths in the world, It is caused by a parasite called plasmodium.
This parasite is spread by mosquitoes. However, not all mosquitoes carry the plasmodium parasite. It
is only the female anopheles mosquito that carries the parasite. A single bite from this type of mosquito
can inject millions of the disease causing parasite into your blood stream.

Apart from causing malaria, mosquito bites can also cause swellings on the skin. These swellings
may become red and itchy and eventually turn into wounds when scratched. Furthermore, mosquitoes
are annoying because they keep us awake at night.

Is there anything we can do to keep away this troublesome insect? Yes, there is. The solution lies
in keeping our environment clean. We can do this by clearing bushes around our houses. We should also
drain stagnant water to prevent mosquitoes from breeding near our homes. Sleeping under mosquito
nets can also help in keeping away this stubborn tiny insect.

All in all, it is possible to prevent malaria by ensuring that mosquitoes do not come into contact
with our bodies.
